claims.text: Adding a low volume fraction of graphene nanoplatelets at W/Cu interfaces will increase the overall thermal conductivity of a W–Cu composite.
Interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will not degrade the mechanical integrity of the W–Cu composite.
Interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will preserve the irradiation resistance of the W–Cu composite.
Dispersing graphene at W/Cu interfaces can form a continuous nanoscale interfacial network.
Spark plasma sintering or an equivalent process can ensure uniform dispersion of graphene in the proposed W–Cu composite.
A continuous graphene network at W/Cu interfaces will enhance interfacial bonding.
A continuous graphene network at W/Cu interfaces will create additional heat-transport pathways.
Graphene has intrinsically very high thermal conductivity.
Graphene has excellent intrinsic mechanical strength.
Graphene at W/Cu interfaces can bridge thermally resistive interfaces through rapid electron and phonon conduction pathways.
Graphene's mechanical durability will help maintain the structural integrity of the W–Cu composite.
Graphene is sufficiently chemically inert in the proposed W–Cu processing and service environments to help maintain structural integrity.
Interfacial graphene will prevent irradiation-induced degradation of the W–Cu composite.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will have significantly higher overall thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable graphene-free W–Cu composite.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain strength comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain ductility comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain irradiation resistance comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
The predicted enhancement will persist under high heat flux, cyclic thermal loading, and irradiation representative of fusion-reactor joints.
Excessive graphene content could cause interfacial brittleness or percolation-related problems.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity improvement will depend on graphene dispersion and interfacial contact.
